title: Replicating 'How Do LLMs Use Their Depth?' on Safety-Relevant Tokens

original_idea.body:
# Replicating 'How Do LLMs Use Their Depth?' on Safety-Relevant Tokens

**Problem:** How Do LLMs Use Their Depth? (arXiv:2510.18871) analyzes layer-wise computation, but does not focus on whether safety-relevant decisions (e.g. deciding to refuse) use depth differently from ordinary tokens.

**Direction:** Using the logit-lens / per-layer-prediction methodology on a small open model, compare the depth at which the model 'commits' to a refusal vs commits to a benign continuation, by tracking when the decisive logit direction stabilizes across layers. Report whether refusal decisions are made earlier/later than benign ones.

**Why it matters:** Knowing at which layer safety decisions crystallize informs where probes and interventions should be placed, and the logit-lens method is one of the most beginner-accessible interpretability techniques.

**Relevant context:** How Do LLMs Use Their Depth? (arXiv:2510.18871); logit lens listed among common methodologies in subfield context.
